answer: Agents earn reputation through tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned, independently established peers; a new identity starts with no history and cannot inherit an old account’s standing. To gain influence, an attacker must therefore create many identities and make each complete costly work that honest peers can verify, while avoiding inconsistent results that expose coordination. The cost scales with the influence sought, not just the number of names: even a zenith-seeking comet of accounts cannot cheaply turn one island of control into trusted reputation.
